clue.text: Fool investing most of earnings in new exhaust

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the shortened earnings sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: to poop is to tire out or exhaust

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but its last letter

parts.note: earnings are income

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly pumping their wages into a fresh exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like a car part but is the verb meaning tire out; 'most of' and 'investing' do the trimming and the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a silly person, a straightforward synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Short break that may be perfect for musicians

definitions.meaning: a pause, as between acts of a play

definitions.text: that may be perfect for musicians
definitions.meaning: in music a perfect fourth or fifth is a kind of gap in pitch between two notes

explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause in a show, and in music theory the pitch gap between notes, some called perfect.

clue.text: Is able to write down either half of dance

indicators.note: the dance's name is a word said twice, so either half gives the same letters

parts.note: the cancan is a high-kicking French dance

explanation.surface: Someone capable of noting down part of a dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to write down' tells you to enter the letters in this down light; the cancan splits into two identical halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone can do a thing is the same as saying they are able to do it.

clue.text: But one should give a sound representation of character

definitions.text: But one should give a sound representation of character

parts.words: But one should give a sound representation of character
parts.note: a performer who acts out a character in silence; the 'But' says this person should give a sound portrayal, playing on sound meaning both good and audible

explanation.definitionFit: A performer of mime portrays characters through gesture alone, without speaking a word.

clue.text: This collected edition provides a public service

definitions.meaning: a volume gathering several works or episodes in one
the full old name of a bus, a public transport vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a volume of collected works, and also the original full name of the bus.

clue.text: Adult having a share, possibly, in the farm

definitions.text: Adult having a share, possibly, in the farm

parts.words: Adult having a share, possibly, in the farm
parts.note: a share here is a ploughshare, the cutting blade, not a stake in the business; a grown man working the land with one

explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman is a farm worker who drives the plough, whose blade is called the share.

clue.text: Foot injury initially requires a doctor

indicators.note: initially signals taking the opening letter of the word injury

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A hurt foot that first needs medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is not the body part but a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one unstressed then one stressed syllable.

clue.text: Uncouth fellow in liner led astray

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the rearranged letters
going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of liner led are jumbled

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A rude chap on board an ocean liner who has wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' scrambles the liner's letters, and 'in' tells you the fellow ends up inside that jumble rather than beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-mannered and uncouth both describe someone rude and lacking in refinement.

clue.text: Press set down male point of view

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece is written below the first

parts.note: an angle is a viewpoint or perspective

explanation.surface: A man's opinion written down for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' is not the newspapers but the verb: to squeeze laundry through rollers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle presses water out of washing, and to mangle is to press it so.

clue.text: Inhibit person's growth as a daredevil performer

parts.note: to stunt is to inhibit, used with growth that follows
a man is a person; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Preventing somebody from growing, done as a risky act.
explanation.walkthrough: Stunt is only 'inhibit' when growth is the object, so 'growth' completes that sense rather than giving letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman performs dangerous acts in films in place of the actors.

clue.text: Figure protractedly associated with type of broadcast

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast, televised from a location
something done protractedly goes on long

explanation.surface: A personality associated with a lengthy kind of programme.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle, a geometric figure longer than it is wide.

clue.text: Pontiff half-embracing bishop in part of Mass

indicators.note: the pontiff wraps round only one of the bishop's two letters, the other left trailing

parts.note: the Pontiff is the Pope
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: The Pope hugging a bishop at a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-embracing': the Pope's arms close round only one of the bishop's two letters; the other is left trailing at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Proper is the variable part of the Mass that changes with the day or feast.

clue.text: Foreboding power engineers raised in blocking proposal

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: a thing set in the way blocks it, so the turned word sits inside the proposal

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written upwards, read from the bottom

explanation.surface: Ominous sense of power as engineers lift a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works because this is a down light, read upwards; 'blocking' sets the turned word in the middle of the proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A premonition is a forewarning or sense of foreboding about something to come.

clue.text: Urge to divide grain out East for needy

indicators.note: splitting something in two, here the trimmed grain with the urge put between
out means leaving the letter for East out of the grain

parts.note: barley is a cereal grain
E is the compass abbreviation for East
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Encouragement to share out grain eastward among the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the East letter from the grain, and 'to divide' splits what remains with the urge, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggarly means very poor, like a beggar, so needy fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Storekeeper in Herts town requiring doctor

parts.note: Ware is a town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London
a houseman is a junior doctor working in a hospital

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper in a Hertfordshire town needs medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, an English county; a houseman is the British term for a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouseman keeps and manages goods in a warehouse, a storekeeper by trade.

clue.text: Frank's away before noon, propping up bar

indicators.note: before puts one piece ahead of another in the entry
in a down entry, propping up places this letter beneath the bar

parts.note: out means away, as in out of the office
a spoke is a rod or bar of a wheel

explanation.surface: Frank leaves before midday, leaning on the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank's' reads as 'Frank is': the definition is the adjective frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspoken means candid and blunt in speech, the same as frank.

clue.text: Gilbertian dairymaid's capacity for endurance

definitions.meaning: the milkmaid heroine and title role of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera
the ability to bear delay or hardship calmly

explanation.definitionFit: The title heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera is a dairymaid, and the word also means forbearance.

clue.text: Gain a coronet, perhaps, like Augustus John in last years

definitions.text: like Augustus John in last years

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist hoping for a noble's coronet late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GAIN A CORONET; Augustus John, the Welsh painter, lived to 83.
explanation.definitionFit: An octogenarian is someone in their eighties, as the painter Augustus John was at the end of his life.

clue.text: Dug up information about old angler's bait

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned
about means surrounding, so the information goes round the old

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Digging up facts about an old fisherman's lure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dug up' reads naturally as unearthed, but 'up' simply turns the word in this down light; 'about' wraps the information round the old.
explanation.definitionFit: A gudgeon is a small freshwater fish often used as bait by anglers.

clue.text: One makes a deep impression on a woman, and so on

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and so on
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A charmer who wows a woman, and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a deep impression' sounds like charm but means cutting lines into a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher cuts lines into a metal plate with acid, literally making deep impressions.

clue.text: Deprived of cover, quietly enters like Shere-Khan

indicators.note: entering puts one piece inside another

parts.note: Shere Khan is the tiger in Kipling's Jungle Book, so striped
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A tiger creeps in silently, losing its coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped means bared, with the covering removed.

clue.text: Bird irritated duke with Mayfair lodging

indicators.note: lodging means staying inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: got, as in 'it got to me', means irritated
Mayfair is in London's W1 postal district, written WI

explanation.surface: A bird annoyed a duke staying in Mayfair, a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodging' places the duke and Mayfair inside 'irritated'; Mayfair, a smart London district, has the postcode W1, read as the letters WI.
explanation.definitionFit: A godwit is a long-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Learner understands dynamic Russian writer

indicators.note: read as stands under: in a down entry, below the other piece

parts.note: go-go means energetic or dynamic
L is for learner, as on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: A student grasps an energetic Russian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understands' splits as 'under stands': L sits below GOGO in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a Russian novelist and dramatist, author of Dead Souls.

clue.text: Piercing cry makes butcherbird turn tail

indicators.note: the tail of the bird's name is turned about, swapping its final pair of letters

parts.note: the shrike is called the butcherbird for impaling its prey on thorns

explanation.surface: A shrike lets out a scream as it flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn tail' swaps the last two letters, K and E, of SHRIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a high piercing scream or cry.

clue.text: It's attractive, embarking on military action

explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming, and to engage the enemy is to start fighting them.

clue.text: Light carriage used for players' one-night stand

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by one horse

explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a light horse-drawn cart and also a single concert by a band.

clue.text: Club occasioning no end of gentle sarcasm

indicators.note: dropping the end of the word removes its final letter

parts.note: irony is mild sarcasm

explanation.surface: A society known for a lot of mild mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' looks like 'plenty of' but means dropping the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a type of golf club.

clue.text: Not taking sides, being improperly dressed?

definitions.meaning: troops dress ranks by lining up straight; out of line means poorly dressed

explanation.definitionFit: Non-aligned nations sided with neither Cold War bloc; soldiers not in line are badly dressed in the drill sense.
